text:
chris: Quick proposal 9: reduce surface for SIEM raw exports. Default retention stays short (7d). Access to raw exports moved behind new 'siem-privileged' role that requires JIT KMS unwrap + ticketed approval. Playback UI stays for 'siem-analyst' (redacted). Thoughts?

priya: strong +1. we should codify who can grant siem-privileged. suggest: security leads + legal + designated incident owners. also need an audit trail that includes key unwrap event and ticket id.

vault-bot: Note: current KMS policy allows GenerateDataKey for service-role only. New flow will require short-lived grants. Recommend KMS 'Grant' + CMK rotation check.

chris: good catch. do we prefer KMS grants via our proxy service or temporary IAM assume-role that holds plaintext key in memory? security implications?

tom: proxy is safer. avoid storing keys in compute. proxy can log unwrapping and limit by TTL and requester ticket. we already have a small KMS-proxy used for ephemeral artifacts. re-use?

priya: reuse preferred. only extra: enforce that the proxy requires a ticket id and approver signature. also add a reason field and link back to ticketing system.

compliance: must include chain-of-custody metadata on every access: actor, timestamp, ticket, justification, approver. Also redact PII at playback by default. Full raw access needs explicit raw_access flag in ticket. Legal holds bypass approver but still audited.

chris: implementation sketch: 1) new IAM role 'siem-privileged' limited to KMS-proxy call and S3 GetObject on forensic-snapshots with tag "hold=1". 2) request flow: ticket -> approver -> proxy grants plaintext key to short-lived handler (no disk). 3) proxy emits audit event to observability + audit-log bucket (immutable). 4) when extension expires, proxy revokes grant and lifecycle deletes object.

tom: quick pseudo:
```bash
# ticket flow triggered
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123:role/siem-proxy-handler --duration-seconds 3600
# proxy requests KMS grant for object key with constraints (principal=siem-proxy-handler, ttl=4h, ticket=12345)
# proxy streams decrypted bytes to viewer service (no persist)
```

priya: one operational risk: what if lifecycle job deletes object during a long-running investigation? need an object-hold tag set atomically before proxy hands key. lifecycle rule should ignore objects with hold tag. hold tag removed automatically when ticket expires.

chris: agree. also add periodic reconciliation job that lists holds and checks expiration vs ticket state to avoid orphan holds.

oncall: runbook note: if logs are unavailable during triage, escalate to sec-oncall and file a Sev ticket. we had a missed case where export perms blocked triage last month. include contact + phone URT in runbook.

sec-bot: Draft policy uploaded: https://redwood.internal/policies/siem-access-jit-kms.md :thumbsup:

compliance: small ask: provide a sample audit record schema we can ingest into SIEM for retention and evidence. fields: event_id, actor, actor_role, ticket_id, action, object_key, cmk_id, grant_id, timestamp, justification, approver, redaction_level.

chris: will post schema. follow-ups: (1) tom to prototype proxy reuse + audit emission spike (ETA 1 week), (2) priya to draft approver matrix and RBAC change PR, (3) oncall to update runbook with escalation path, (4) compliance to confirm audit schema. sync eng-security Fri.

vault-bot: Reminder: CMK rotation scheduled in 30 days. validate that rotation will not break existing grants.

priya: thanks. if rotation conflicts, we should plan emergency wallet to rewrap objects or short extension window.

chris: cool. I'll create the GH issue and a short sequence diagram. Any other objections?

tom: none from me.

compliance: no objections from compliance side.

chris: closing for now. meeting Friday invite incoming.
